  "source": "Man Group",
  "title": "GLP-1s: A Health Revolution at What Cost?",
  "type": "macro",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-16",
  "insights": [
   "GLP-1 receptor agonists represent a structural shift in population health that may rival statins in their potential to extend lifespans, creating a significant, underpriced longevity risk for financial systems.",
   "The financial impact is asymmetric: longer lifespans immediately increase pension and annuity obligations, while potential productivity gains from improved healthspan accrue only over decades, if at all.",
   "Healthcare systems face a 'prevention paradox' where shifting from acute, episodic care to continuous, front-loaded pharmaceutical spending may reshape the cost curve rather than lower it.",
   "A structural funding dilemma exists in fragmented systems like the US, where private insurers bear the drug costs while public systems (Medicare/Medicaid) accrue the long-term savings from avoided late-life care.",
   "Actuarial models currently rely on historical mortality data and may be caught by surprise by the rapid adoption of GLP-1s, potentially leading to a 'longevity catastrophe' for underfunded pension and insurance liabilities.",
   "Emerging markets like China and India, with large overweight populations and weaker public-health financing, may experience the systemic longevity signal and fiscal impact before developed markets.",
   "Investors should monitor prescription volumes, adherence rates (currently low, with ~53.6% discontinuation at one year), and the generic pipeline as key indicators of the scale of the longevity shock.",
   "The patent waterfall for GLP-1s is expected to run from 2035 to 2040, which will likely trigger a second phase of systemic risk as lower-cost generic versions broaden access to less affluent populations."
